title: Machine Learning Time Series Forecasting: A Comprehensive Survey and Stock Market Application
venue: University of Georgia, Master of Science Thesis
tldr: Surveys top-performing ML methods for time series prediction and applies LightGBM with engineered features to day trading, achieving returns several orders above human traders.
problem_and_motivation: Time series prediction across domains lacks meaningful model comparisons due to heterogeneous experimental setups. Day trading, constrained by human cognitive limits, requires automated systems that can process large-scale tick data.
approach: Conducted a comprehensive survey of 79 papers comparing tree-based and deep learning methods under identical experimental conditions from Web of Science.
Applied LightGBM models with extensive feature engineering across multi-timeframe technical indicators and contextual stock attributes.
Used two years of second-by-second trade and quote data from all U.S. equities to estimate risk-reward ratios over multiple forward time horizons.
Simulated day trading with realistic execution constraints including transaction costs and market impact.
Evaluated performance against human day trader benchmarks using daily returns as the primary metric.
findings: num: LightGBM-based model yielded daily returns several orders of magnitude higher than human day traders.
Tree-based methods like LightGBM and deep learning methods like RNN deliver best time series forecasting performance.
Tree-based methods offer significant computational efficiency advantages over deep learning approaches.
Feature engineering with multi-timeframe indicators was critical for prediction performance in day trading.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This thesis provides a structured survey that enables direct comparison of tree-based and deep learning methods for time series prediction, filling a gap caused by heterogeneous experimental setups in prior reviews. It demonstrates that LightGBM with engineered features can outperform human traders in day trading, establishing a benchmark for ML-based financial forecasting. The work establishes practical recommendations for model selection based on dataset size, task type, and computational budget.
directly_justifies: Tree-based and deep learning methods both deliver top performance in time series forecasting.
LightGBM-based day trading model achieved returns exceeding human traders by orders of magnitude.
Computational efficiency favors tree-based methods for production forecasting systems.
limits: Day trading application is specific to high-frequency equity markets, not personal budget forecasting.
Survey covers 2017-2024 but LLM-based forecasting methods are not included.
Real-world trading results are simulated with assumed execution constraints.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 topic domains was performed. Domain 6 (Predictive Modeling and Forecasting) was flagged as high relevance because the paper's core contribution is ML time series forecasting methodology and its application to financial data. Domain 7 (Budgeting) received low relevance as day trading differs from personal budget recommendation but shares constrained optimization concepts. All other domains (1-5, 8-14) were rejected as the paper does not address demographics, financial behavior, expense categorization, anomaly detection, mobile UX, privacy, engagement, evaluation frameworks, savings, synthetic data, or ML serving. Borderline case: Domain 7.C was included at low relevance because risk-reward optimization in trading parallels constrained budget allocation.

limitations: Simulated trading results may not replicate in live markets due to slippage and execution uncertainty.
Survey limited to papers comparing both TBML and DL within the same experimental setup. [unacknowledged]
LightGBM model performance may degrade under different market regimes not present in training data.
remember_this: LightGBM outperforms human day traders by orders of magnitude in simulated trading.
Tree-based methods offer competitive accuracy with significantly lower computational cost than DL.
Survey of 79 papers provides practical model selection guidelines for time series tasks.
Feature engineering with multi-timeframe indicators is critical for financial time series prediction.
